meanings: to be, to exist, to live
to have
to be located
to be equipped with
to happen, to come about

examples.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
examples.furigana: 机[つくえ]の 上[うえ]に 本[ほん]があります。
examples.english: There is a book on the desk.

usage_notes: Used for the existence of inanimate things, plants, and events (パーティーがある). For people and animals, use いる instead. The plain negative is irregular: ない / ありません, never あらない. The thing that exists is marked with が, and the place with に.

meanings: to be (of animate objects), to exist
to stay
to be ...-ing, to have been ...-ing

examples.japanese: 妹は今、家にいます。
examples.furigana: 妹[いもうと]は 今[いま]、 家[いえ]にいます。
examples.english: My little sister is at home right now.

usage_notes: いる is used for people and animals; use ある for inanimate things (本があります). The polite forms are います／いません, and the past is いました／いませんでした. Attached to a て-form it makes the progressive: 食べています (is eating). Note it is a る-verb (ichidan), so the negative is いない, not いらない.

meanings: to do, to carry out, to perform
to cause to become, to make (into), to turn (into)
to serve as, to act as, to work as
to wear (clothes, a facial expression, etc.)
to judge as being, to view as being, to think of as, to treat as, to use as
to decide on, to choose
to be sensed (of a smell, noise, etc.)
to be (in a state, condition, etc.)
to be worth, to cost
to pass (of time), to elapse
to place, or raise, person A to a post or status B
to transform A to B, to make A into B, to exchange A for B
to make use of A for B, to view A as B, to handle A as if it were B
to feel A about B
verbalizing suffix (applies to nouns noted in this dictionary with the part of speech "vs")
creates a humble verb (after a noun prefixed with "o" or "go")
to be just about to, to be just starting to, to try to, to attempt to

examples.japanese: 週末は何をしますか。
examples.furigana: 週末[しゅうまつ]は 何[なに]をしますか。
examples.english: What are you doing this weekend?

usage_notes: Irregular verb: します／しない／した／して, potential できる. It attaches to many nouns to make verbs (勉強する, 練習する, コピーする); with those, you can often say either 勉強します or 勉強をします, the version with を feeling slightly more like 'do some studying'. Note that 何をする uses を, while 'become' senses use に (医者にする).

meanings: to be able (in a position) to do, to be up to the task
to be ready, to be completed
to be made, to be built
to be good at, to be permitted (to do)
to become intimate, to take up (with somebody)
to grow, to be raised
to become pregnant

examples.japanese: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.furigana: 日本語[にほんご]が 少[すこ]しできます。
examples.english: I can speak a little Japanese.

usage_notes: The thing you can do is marked with が, not を: 日本語ができる, 料理ができる. With a verb, use the pattern 〜ことができる (話すことができる = to be able to speak). It is intransitive, so there is no を before できる. Also very common in the sense "to be finished/ready" (ご飯ができました) and "to be built" (新しい駅ができた); the past できた often means "it's done."

meanings: to become, to get, to grow, to turn, to reach, to attain
to result in, to turn out, to end up, to prove (to be)
to consist of, to be composed of, to be made up of
to be completed, to be realized, to succeed, to be attained, to be accomplished
to change (into), to turn (into), to transform
to come (to do), to begin (to do), to grow (to do)
to come to, to amount to, to add up to, to make
to play (the part of), to act as
to be used for, to be useful for, to serve as
to be promoted
to do ...

examples.japanese: 兄はエンジニアになりました。
examples.furigana: 兄[あに]はエンジニアになりました。
examples.english: My older brother became an engineer.

usage_notes: Nouns and な-adjectives take に before なる (エンジニアになる, 有名になる), while い-adjectives change to the く form instead (安くなる, 大きくなる). Learners often say ×大きいになる by mistake.

meanings: to use (a thing, method, etc.), to make use of, to put to use
to use (a person, animal, puppet, etc.), to employ, to handle, to manage, to manipulate
to use (time, money, etc.), to spend, to consume
to use (language), to speak

examples.japanese: 仕事でこのソフトを使います。
examples.furigana: 仕事[しごと]でこのソフトを 使[つか]います。
examples.english: I use this software for work.

examples.japanese: そのペン、ちょっと使ってもいい？
examples.furigana: そのペン、ちょっと 使[つか]ってもいい？
examples.english: Can I use that pen for a sec?

usage_notes: Transitive, so the thing used takes を: パソコンを使う. It covers tools, money, and time (お金を使う "spend money", 時間を使う "spend time"), and also languages (日本語を使う). Potential form is 使える ("can use / usable"), which is very common: このカードは使えますか。

meanings: to understand, to comprehend, to grasp, to see, to get, to follow
to become clear, to be known, to be discovered, to be realized, to be realised, to be found out
I know!, I think so too!

examples.japanese: この漢字の意味が分かりません。
examples.furigana: この 漢字[かんじ]の 意味[いみ]が 分[わ]かりません。
examples.english: I don't understand the meaning of this kanji.

usage_notes: The thing understood is marked with が, not を: 日本語が分かる. It is intransitive and describes a state, so 分かります often translates as "I understand" rather than an action. Alone, 分かった／分かりました means "got it, understood."

meanings: to think, to consider, to believe, to reckon
to think (of doing), to plan (to do)
to judge, to assess, to regard
to imagine, to suppose, to dream
to expect, to look forward to
to feel, to be (in a state of mind), to desire, to want
to recall, to remember

examples.japanese: 明日は雨が降ると思います。
examples.furigana: 明日[あした]は 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]ると 思[おも]います。
examples.english: I think it will rain tomorrow.

usage_notes: Almost always used as ...と思う: the thought or opinion comes first in plain (short) form, followed by と思います, even when the rest of the sentence is polite. 思う is transitive and takes を with noun objects (何を思っていますか), but for stating opinions the と pattern is the normal one. For present-moment thoughts about oneself, 思っている is also common (ずっとそう思っています, "I've thought so all along").

meanings: to write, to compose, to pen
to draw, to paint

examples.japanese: 友だちに手紙を書きました。
examples.furigana: 友[とも]だちに 手紙[てがみ]を 書[か]きました。
examples.english: I wrote a letter to my friend.

usage_notes: Everyday word for writing text: 手紙を書く, メールを書く, 名前を書く. As a godan verb the て-form is 書いて (not 書きて), and the past is 書いた. When you mean drawing a picture, the usual spelling is 描く (かく/えがく), though 絵をかく is often left in kana.

meanings: to come (spatially or temporally), to approach, to arrive
to come back, to do ... and come back
to come to be, to become, to get, to grow, to continue
to come from, to be caused by, to derive from
to come to (i.e. "when it comes to spinach ...")

examples.japanese: 友だちが来週、東京に来ます。
examples.furigana: 友[とも]だちが 来週[らいしゅう]、 東京[とうきょう]に 来[き]ます。
examples.english: My friend is coming to Tokyo next week.

usage_notes: 来る is one of the two irregular verbs (with する). Note the shifting stem readings: 来ます (きます), 来ない (こない), 来て (きて), 来た (きた), 来られる (こられる). It attaches to the て-form of other verbs to mean "go and do something, then come back": 買ってくる (buy it and come back), 行ってきます (I'm off / I'll be back).

meanings: to be aware of, to know, to be conscious of, to cognize, to cognise
to notice, to feel
to understand, to comprehend, to grasp
to remember, to be acquainted with (a procedure)
to experience, to go through, to learn
to be acquainted with (a person), to get to know
to concern

examples.japanese: あの人の名前を知っていますか。
examples.furigana: あの 人[ひと]の 名前[なまえ]を 知[し]っていますか。
examples.english: Do you know that person's name?

usage_notes: To say you currently know something, use the ている form 知っている(知っています) — plain 知る means "to come to know, to find out". The negative is irregular in practice: say 知らない/知りません, not 知っていない. Compare 分かる, which is about understanding or figuring something out rather than having the information.

meanings: to hear
to listen (e.g. to music)
to ask, to enquire, to query
to hear about, to hear of, to learn of
to follow (advice, order, etc.), to obey, to listen to, to comply with
to hear (e.g. a plea), to grant (a request), to accept (e.g. an argument), to give consideration to
to smell (esp. incense), to sample (a fragrance)
to taste (alcohol), to try

examples.japanese: 毎朝、電車で音楽を聞きます。
examples.furigana: 毎朝[まいあさ]、 電車[でんしゃ]で 音楽[おんがく]を 聞[き]きます。
examples.english: Every morning I listen to music on the train.

usage_notes: Covers both "listen/hear" and "ask". When it means "ask", the person asked is marked with に: 先生に聞きます (I'll ask the teacher). The thing heard or asked about takes を. 聴く is a variant kanji used specifically for listening attentively (music, etc.), but 聞く is the safe default.

meanings: to go

examples.japanese: 家族と城崎温泉に行きました。
examples.furigana: 家族[かぞく]と 城崎温泉[きのさきおんせん]に 行[い]きました。
examples.romaji: Kazoku to Kinosaki Onsen ni ikimashita.
examples.english: I went to Kinosaki Onsen with my family.

usage_notes: Godan verb, but its て-form and past are irregular: 行って / 行った (not 行いて). The place you go to is marked with に or へ; the purpose with に after a noun or verb stem (買い物に行く). Also read ゆく in more literary or set expressions.

meanings: to see, to look, to watch, to view, to observe
to examine, to look over, to assess, to check, to judge
to look after, to attend to, to take care of, to keep an eye on
to experience, to meet with (misfortune, success, etc.)
to try ..., to have a go at ..., to give ... a try
to see (that) ..., to find (that) ...

examples.japanese: 昨日、家で映画を見ました。
examples.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、 家[いえ]で 映画[えいが]を 見[み]ました。
examples.english: Yesterday I watched a movie at home.

usage_notes: Ichidan verb: 見ます, 見て, 見た, 見ない. Use 見る for actively looking or watching (TV, movies, sights); 見える means something is visible without effort on your part. As an auxiliary after the て-form it means "try doing" (食べてみる = try eating) and is normally written in kana: 〜てみる.

meanings: to say, to utter, to declare
to name, to call
to go (e.g. "the alarm went ping"), to make a noise

examples.japanese: 友だちは「また明日」と言いました。
examples.furigana: 友[とも]だちは「また 明日[あした]」と 言[い]いました。
examples.english: My friend said, "See you tomorrow."

usage_notes: Although written 言う, the plain form is normally pronounced "yū" in speech (the past 言った is "itta"). Quoted or reported speech is marked with と before 言う: 「…」と言いました, or 明日行くと言いました ("he said he would go tomorrow"). Use 言う for the act of saying words; 話す is for talking/speaking with someone.

meanings: to speak
to talk

examples.japanese: 毎日、妻と日本語で話します。
examples.furigana: 毎日[まいにち]、妻[つま]と 日本語[にほんご]で 話[はな]します。
examples.english: I speak Japanese with my wife every day.

examples.japanese: 昨日、田中さんと電話で話したんだ。
examples.furigana: 昨日[きのう]、田中[たなか]さんと 電話[でんわ]で 話[はな]したんだ。
examples.english: I talked with Tanaka on the phone yesterday.

usage_notes: Use it for speaking or talking. The person spoken with is often marked by と.

meanings: to read
to recite (e.g. a sutra), to chant
to predict, to guess, to forecast, to read (someone's thoughts), to see (e.g. into someone's heart), to divine
to decipher
to count, to estimate
to read (a kanji) with its native Japanese reading

examples.japanese: この本はもう読みましたか。
examples.furigana: この 本[ほん]はもう 読[よ]みましたか。
examples.english: Have you already read this book?

usage_notes: Everyday word for reading, whether aloud or silently; the thing read takes を (本を読む、新聞を読む). Godan, so the て-form is 読んで and the past is 読んだ. The potential 読める is very common for "can read / is legible".

meanings: to buy, to purchase
to value, to have a high opinion
to stir, to provoke, to draw upon oneself

examples.japanese: 駅の前のスーパーで野菜を買います。
examples.furigana: 駅[えき]の 前[まえ]のスーパーで 野菜[やさい]を 買[か]います。
examples.english: I buy vegetables at the supermarket in front of the station.

usage_notes: Everyday word for buying: 〜を買う, with the place marked by で (スーパーで買う). As a godan verb: 買います / 買わない / 買った / 買って. Note the わ in the negative 買わない, not 買あない. The extra meanings ('to value highly', as in 高く買う, or 'to provoke', as in 恨みを買う) are set phrases you can leave for later.

meanings: to eat

examples.japanese: クリスマスに家族と韓国料理を食べます。
examples.furigana: クリスマスに 家族[かぞく]と 韓国料理[かんこくりょうり]を 食[た]べます。
examples.romaji: Kurisumasu ni kazoku to Kankoku ryouri o tabemasu.
examples.english: At Christmas, I eat Korean food with my family.

usage_notes: Regular ichidan verb: 食べる → 食べます、食べない、食べて. Takes を for the thing eaten. Note that Japanese uses 飲む (to drink) rather than 食べる for soup and similar liquids, e.g. スープを飲む.

meanings: to drink, to gulp, to swallow, to take (medicine)
to smoke (tobacco)
to engulf, to overwhelm
to keep down, to suppress
to accept (e.g. demand, condition)
to make light of, to conceal

examples.japanese: いっしょにお茶を飲みませんか。
examples.furigana: いっしょにお 茶[ちゃ]を 飲[の]みませんか。
examples.english: Would you like to have some tea with me?

examples.japanese: 薬を飲んでから、寝ます。
examples.furigana: 薬[くすり]を 飲[の]んでから、 寝[ね]ます。
examples.english: I'll take my medicine and then go to bed.

usage_notes: Everyday word for drinking. Note that Japanese uses 飲む (not 食べる) for taking medicine: 薬を飲む. On its own, 飲む often implies drinking alcohol — 飲みに行く means "to go out drinking." Godan verb: 飲みます / 飲まない / 飲んだ / 飲んで.
